subject: AI & Agents
title: The Context Window: LLM Memory
description: A quick, practical guide to The Context Window: LLM Memory.

hook.text: Ask an LLM about something you said 50 messages ago. If it's outside the window, it's gone.

buildup.text: The context window is the maximum number of tokens an LLM can process at once.

discovery.text: GPT-4 Turbo handles 128,000 tokens. Claude handles 200,000. Earlier models had just 2,048.

twist.text: Bigger windows use more memory and compute. Cost scales quadratically with window size.

climax.text: New techniques like sliding windows and retrieval augmentation help work around limits.

punchline.text: LLMs don't remember. They just have a really long scratchpad.

quiz.question: What limits how much text an LLM can consider at once?
options: The context window size in tokens
The speed of the internet connection

details.summary: The context window is the maximum amount of text an LLM can consider at once. Early models handled 2,000 tokens; modern models support 100,000 or more, enabling analysis of entire documents and long conversations.
details.whyItMatters: Context window size determines what an LLM can do. Small windows forget earlier conversation. Large windows enable document analysis, code understanding, and sustained complex reasoning.
takeaways: The context window limits how much text an LLM processes at once
Larger windows enable longer conversations and document analysis
Memory beyond the context window is effectively lost

faq.question: What happens when conversation exceeds the context window?
faq.answer: The oldest tokens are dropped from the model's input. The model literally forgets the beginning of the conversation. This is why long chats can lose coherence — the model no longer sees what was discussed earlier.

faq.question: How are context windows getting larger?
faq.answer: Techniques like RoPE scaling, sliding window attention, and efficient attention algorithms have extended windows from 2K to 200K+ tokens. Google's Gemini 1.5 supports a million tokens in research settings.
